market.title: House votes to curb AI data center costs
market.summary: The House passed the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act on Wednesday, marking Congress' most significant step yet to shield consumers from the soaring infrastructure costs of the AI boom . Why it matters: Washington is facing growing pressure to put guardrails around AI's rapid expansion, from the technology itself to the data centers powering it. The bipartisan bill, which passed 417-3, would require state utility regulators to consider rules making data centers cover some of the costs of new power generation. Its passage gives lawmakers a tangible response to an issue that has quickly become a political flashpoint ahead of the midterms. Driving the news: The vote comes amid a broader reckoning over the pace and costs of AI development. Last weekend, leaders of some of the world's most powerful AI companies called for slowing the development of frontier AI models to give safety measures time to catch up. Data centers have become a focus of anti-AI sentiment, with 70% of Americans opposing construction in their area. Lawmakers in both parties have backed efforts to slow or restrict data center development amid concerns about electricity bills, strained power grids and water use. Catch up quick: The bill, led by Reps. Gabe Evans (R-Colo.) and Kathy Castor (D-Fla.), advanced out of the House Energy and Commerce Committee in July. GOP leadership had been previously non-committal about bringing it to the floor. The intrigue: The House's move comes as President Trump is arguing against pumping the brakes on AI development, framing U.S. dominance in the technology as a race against China. The only control or "guardrails" that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" the president posted Monday on Truth Social. Trump has also aggressively defended data center development amid growing local backlash, saying in an Aug. 31 Truth Social post that communities that reject the facilities will be "backwards and poor." "If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign," Trump wrote. What to watch: Trump's comments have put him at odds with some Republicans who have sought to distance themselves from data centers as the issue becomes increasingly salient in the midterms.

LSF.title: Can Chefs' Warehouse's Pricing Execution Keep Lifting Margins?
LSF.summary: The Chefs' Warehouse improved its Q2 gross margin by 49 basis points to 25.1% through investments in pricing teams, procurement capabilities, and AI-based technology. Despite 4.9% net product cost inflation, the company achieved 15.2% gross profit growth, outpacing 12.9% net sales growth. The stock has surged 62.2% over the past year.

INOD.title: Innodata's Customer Diversification Effort: Is It Finally Paying Off?
INOD.summary: Innodata achieved 58% revenue growth to $92.1M in Q2 2026, marking its 12th consecutive quarter of growth. The company successfully reduced customer concentration, with its largest customer dropping from 56% to 37% of revenues, while a Big Tech customer scaled to 34%. Adjusted gross margins expanded to 49% and adjusted EBITDA jumped 92%, though the top two customers still account for 71% of revenues. INOD trades at a premium valuation with a forward P/E of 35.67 and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

CL.title: Can Colgate Revive North America Growth in the Second Half?
CL.summary: Colgate-Palmolive (CL) is addressing weak North America performance in Q2 2026 caused by soft category trends, competitive pressure, and retailer destocking. The company plans to boost premium toothpaste products, expand Fabuloso, increase advertising spending, and implement targeted pricing to drive market-share recovery in the second half of 2026. Management expects sequential improvement but cautioned recovery will be uneven and dependent on consumer demand health.

CL.title: Can Procter & Gamble's Fabric & Home Care Segment Regain Momentum?
CL.summary: Procter & Gamble's Fabric & Home Care segment shows early improvement with Tide original liquid shifting to high-single-digit growth following a major product upgrade, while Tide evo and fabric enhancers offer future growth potential. However, European competition remains intense and Home Care faces headwinds. Church & Dwight and Colgate-Palmolive are also sustaining momentum through innovation and brand strength, though competitive pressures and uneven consumer demand persist across the household care sector.

BLK.title: Will Truist's Prime Auto Lending Exit Strengthen Its Profitability?
BLK.summary: Truist Financial is selling $5.5 billion in near-prime auto loans from its Regional Acceptance Corporation (RAC) subsidiary as new CEO Mike Lyons implements a strategic portfolio review. The transaction, expected to close in late Q3 or early Q4 2026, will improve Truist's credit profile, reduce non-performing loans by over 10 basis points, and generate approximately $945 million in CET1 capital. The bank plans to redeploy resources toward core banking, payments, cards, and mortgage products.

BLK.title: Are You Looking for a High-Growth Dividend Stock?

DSNKY.title: Avacta Achieves Clinical Proof of Mechanism for the Next Generation of pre|CISION® Medicines with AVA6103 (FAP-Exd) in the Phase 1 FOCUS-01 Trial
DSNKY.summary: Avacta announced positive Phase 1 clinical data for AVA6103, its next-generation FAP-targeted peptide-drug conjugate, demonstrating a clean safety profile with controlled-release exatecan at doses 50% higher than conventional exatecan's MTD. Pharmacokinetic data aligned with preclinical predictions, and head-to-head preclinical comparisons showed AVA6103 delivered superior antitumor activity compared to marketed ADC Enhertu®, with deep and durable responses in all treated animals.

ELBM.title: Electra Advances Phased Nickel Refining and Battery Recycling Strategy for North America

The first phase would produce approximately 20,000 tonnes per year of contained nickel with 97%+ recovery rates. Capital estimates range from US$530-675 million, with a potential second phase adding another 20,000 tonnes annually. The facility aims to strengthen North American critical minerals supply chains and reduce reliance on Chinese processing.

ELBM.title: Electra Receives Extension from NASDAQ to Resolve Minimum Price Requirement

The company must achieve a closing bid price at or above US$1.00 for 10 consecutive business days to regain compliance. An unprecedented scenario could unfold if Chair Kevin Warsh opposes the hike while the committee votes to raise rates—the first time in Fed history a sitting chair could be outvoted on monetary policy. The delisting is driven by disproportionate compliance costs, limited trading volume, and the company's reduced need for public equity market access after debt paydown.
